batch_strategy: Select 32 experiments that resolve endpoint-specific solvent-response curves, boundaries on chemical transfer, and a recorded loading-solvent-volume interaction. Use matched comparisons where they distinguish competing explanations, while limiting follow-up of irregular records. All selected IDs and supplied premeasurement predictions are frozen in the reasons below. Scientific questions are expressed directly without formal hypothesis records.

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes narrow several previous interpretations. For m125, the 0/1 completion difference between 500 and 300 ul DCM is 10.89 mL at 100-ul sample loading, contradicting the proposed disappearance under strong eluent. At 5/1, completion differs by only about 0.63 mL at that loading, although onset differs substantially. I therefore retain a conditional recorded association and test its repeatability at a second loading. The m75 20/1-to-50/1 decline at 50 ul did not transfer to 150 ul: the latter endpoints increased from 16.97/34.91 to 37.94/51.52 mL. A general reversal is unsupported, while loading interaction versus record variability remains unresolved. For m58, measured endpoints increased from 6.33/11.48 at 5/1 to 13.50/22.94 at 20/1, supporting the interpretation that the previous predicted reversal and completion plateau were interpolation artifacts. The large historical overpredictions for m201 and m104 at 50/1 further reject a shared positive correction across polar scaffolds. Historical underpredictions at m141, m216 and m205 at 2/1 preserve the case for scaffold-specific early transitions. m194 retained early onset but broad, nonmonotone completion across measured conditions, motivating a second-loading comparison. The accurate m164/m165 20/1 comparison supports connectivity-specific transfer; the shallow m91 response and moderate m73 50/1 result reinforce ester-family boundaries. The m0 completion maximum and m132/m136 2/1 bumps were not supported by their new labels. These error statements concern acquisition-time predictions, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch covers 20 molecules through compact local questions. The m125 pair tests a recorded loading-solvent-volume association, and one m177 experiment follows an irregular loading region without attempting to explain every conflicting record causally. Matched solvent comparisons constrain response amplitude or curvature for dialdehydes, oxygenated aldehydes, an ether-only aromatic scaffold, fused ketones, esters, a nitroketone and a secondary alcohol. The m166/m167 comparison tests structural transfer under identical recorded conditions. Early basic-heteroaromatic anchors and the m159, m181 and m89 points fill consequential gaps between existing measurements. Including moderate branches and strong-eluent anchors alongside predicted later branches should teach where retention corrections stop as well as where growth begins. Several selected families recur extensively in the candidate pool, giving these local relationships potential value across the Row-distribution. No duplicate experimental tuple is selected within the batch, and no pending experiments exist. CW distance and quantile widths are supplied predictor signals rather than calibrated epistemic uncertainty; elution interval width is not uncertainty. Loading amount remains density times sample volume. Recorded contrasts establish associations, with missing experimental information limiting causal interpretation. The expected benefit is better structure-condition interaction learning for both endpoints after retraining.
